title: Local Modulus of Survivor Average Causal Effects near Complementary Survival Margins
banked_reason: D0.5 terminal below floor: general referee tier subfield, score 6.6 below field threshold 7.4; subcritical branch-adaptive honest attainment remains open and three panel findings remain unrepaired; mathematical soundness not established by this review.
gap_reasons: The delivered local-optimality result is confined to indices theta >= c/n: the projection band is matched to the primitive local modulus there, whereas law-local attainment in the genuinely subcritical regime n theta -> 0 remains open in oeq:branch-adaptive-band.
The subcritical theorems characterize a deterministic clipped-box modulus and its sequential limits, not the expected width achievable by a data-driven honest band.
The lower bound is also localized to laws with survival, mean, and moment slack, and the two-cell framework plus deferred ABC application limits the paper's broader econometric significance.
proof_attempt_summary: The D0 solver developed a deterministic clipped-corner modulus profile and a proof outline for matched projection-band width when theta >= c/n. D0.5 judged the delivered package subfield, below the required field floor, because branch-adaptive honest attainment below 1/n remains open. Three panel findings were left unrepaired, and this review did not establish mathematical soundness; no Lean formalization was attempted.
tldr: The published odds-ratio SACE formula becomes a population-weighted ratio of two weak quadratic roots when survival margins approach complementarity. The theorem kernel now gives an all-positive-index modulus decomposition, a computable finite-\(n\) clipped-corner profile valid uniformly through transition and clipping faces, fixed positive-part, square-root, and inverse-gap limits only when the relevant sequential drifts determine them, and a two-scale classification of root-\(n\), intermediate shrinking, and persistent local widths. A finite-sample projection band and a slack-law lower bound provide incremental support, but the current band is not proved law-locally rate matched below \(1/n\); branch-adaptive attainment remains the open-ended question.
gap: Tong, Kahan, Harhay, and Li provide the identifying quadratic root and regular fixed-index inference, while the predecessor supplies causal identification, finite rectangle endpoints, and an above-cutoff growth argument. Neither source gives the population-weighted subcritical branch profile or the exact two-scale classification based on the actual sequence \(H_{\delta,n}\mathcal W_n\).
fill: The project establishes the all-index modulus decomposition, the \(\theta=o(1/n)\) branch profile, and the corrected two-scale frontier. It records honest projection and converse results as support and leaves law-local adaptive attainment below \(1/n\) open.
